tasks.name: Detection
tasks.desc: Is an earthquake present in a 30-second window? Trained on the 19 stations that stream live, with the P onset anywhere in the window and the old system's own false alarms as hard negatives. Chronological held-out test of 7,303 windows (4,964 events): AUC 0.9998, MCC 0.886; STA/LTA on the same filtered input reaches 0.816.

tasks.name: Magnitude
tasks.desc: Network magnitude from multi-station 3-component traces aligned on picked P arrivals, with distances from the located epicentre. 5-seed ensemble R² 0.951 (MAE 0.10) on 937 held-out events (M2-5.2) vs 0.886 for amplitude + distance; in live-like conditions (10 km location error, 3-6 stations) R² 0.939.

tasks.name: Early warning · shaking level
tasks.desc: From the first 8 seconds of P-wave, predict the peak ground velocity that arrives later. Ties the physics baseline on the continuous value. (EEW is offline evidence from the earlier 10-station dataset; not yet retrained on the live network.)

tasks.name: Early warning · alert
tasks.desc: Will shaking exceed a notable threshold? With the alert trigger tuned on validation for recall, the deep model catches 76% of strong-shaking events (up from 65%) at 82% precision. The baseline reaches similar recall only by false-alarming twice as often, so on balanced alert quality (MCC) the deep model wins 0.76 vs 0.66. (EEW is offline evidence from the earlier 10-station dataset; not yet retrained on the live network.)

disclaimer: Research prototype on real California network data, not an operational warning system. The project's original geomagnetic earthquake-precursor forecast was retired after honest validation showed no out-of-sample signal; it pivoted to seismic-waveform deep learning, where the same architecture works. Short-term earthquake prediction (whether one will occur) remains unsolved - this does detection, characterization, and seconds-ahead shaking estimation.
